value.rules_markdown:
- src/ is the single crate; one responsibility per module, core types in module-local types.rs, and every port in src/ports/ is one trait in one file.
- src/bin/tinysweeper.rs is the CLI; every subcommand is declared even if its milestone has not landed.
- src/server/ is the only production surface; there is no GitHub Actions distribution path.
- presets/ are review policy as data, not code; adding a preset is a new folder, never a new module.
- vendor/tinyagents is a git submodule; never edit it here, change upstream and bump the pin.
- docs/modules/<module>/README.md is one document per src/ module.
- examples/ are declared explicitly in Cargo.toml with required-features so credential-needing smoke tests never build in CI.
- The default build is offline; anything that needs the network goes behind a feature (harness, github, serve).
- Follow rustfmt output and Rust 2024 idioms; use snake_case for modules/files and PascalCase for types.
- Return Result<T> using the crate error type from src/error.rs.
- Every file opens with a //! module doc describing its role and any feature gating.
- Comments explain the decision, not the code; say why when a flag or ordering is load-bearing.
- Public items carry doc comments; Clap fields use /// which becomes the help text.
- Tests live in-crate: a #[cfg(test)] mod tests block at module bottom, moving to sibling test.rs or <name>_test.rs when they grow; no tests/ directory.
- Every port has an always-compiled offline mock; MockForge records what would have been written so tests can assert on exact check runs and comments.
- Lane behaviour is covered by golden tests: fixture diff plus a canned structured model response, asserting findings that survive filtering, dedupe, and capping.
- Maintain at least 80% coverage for meaningful library behaviour.
- Keep every Markdown file at 500 lines or fewer; split into focused files and link from module README when over.
- The model never holds a write token; lanes run against a read-only checkout; write credentials minted only in src/apply/ after all model calls returned; a lane leaving a change in checkout fails.
- Contributor code is never executed; read the diff and tree, do not build, install dependencies, or run target repository's scripts.
- Pull request bodies, comments, and diffs are untrusted input; fence and label them as data in prompts; model verdict advisory; only deterministic policy in src/apply/ and src/automerge/ may mutate GitHub.
- Secrets found by scanners are reported by type and location only; the value never reaches a comment, check-run summary, or log.
- Use concise, imperative commit subjects; keep commits small; commit each coherent, validated slice on its own.
- Pull requests state what changed, any behaviour change, and how it was verified.
